extracted.intended_audience: aspiring contributors, editors, and readers of The Best American anthologies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and descriptive rules governing which works are eligible for inclusion in The Best American anthology series and how selections are made each year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: language / translation
rubrics_metrics.description: A work is eligible for the series if it is published in English (or published in another language but translated into English by the author).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'A work is eligible for the series if it is published in English (or published in another language but translated into English by the author) ...' Implication: translations are acceptable only when translated into English by the author (translations by other parties are not specified as eligible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: geographic publication
rubrics_metrics.description: A work is eligible if it is published in the United States, Canada, Mexico, or Greenland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original list of eligible publication countries: United States, Canada, Mexico, or Greenland. This limits the pool of source publications considered for inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: timing / prior-year publication or revision
rubrics_metrics.description: A work is eligible if it first appeared, or was significantly revised, during the previous year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editions feature works that were published during the prior year (e.g., The Best American Essays 2000 contains works published in 1999). The 'significantly revised' clause allows revised pieces that originally appeared earlier to be considered if substantially changed in the relevant year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: author residency / origin
rubrics_metrics.description: A work is eligible if the author comes from or chiefly lives in North America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The series limits eligible authors to those who are from or chiefly resident in North America, tying contributor eligibility to the author's geographic origin/residence as well as the publication venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: internet/publication audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet publications are eligible if their audience includes North American readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'Internet publications are eligible if their audience includes North American readers.' This treats online venues as eligible provided their readership reaches the relevant geographic audience, rather than excluding online-only publications outright.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process: roles of series editor and guest editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Each title has a continuing series editor who makes an initial selection of notable works from which a guest editor chooses those for inclusion in that year's edition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Series editor performs initial curation; guest editor (an established author in the title's genre) makes final selections. A new guest editor is chosen each year. This two-stage process determines which pieces make the anthology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition for non-selected works: honorable mentions
rubrics_metrics.description: Works that do not make the final cut are often given honorable mention in an alphabetical list at the back of the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a piece is not included in the anthology's main selections, it may be acknowledged via an honorable-mention list; these are usually presented alphabetically in the back matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication schedule / edition timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Editions are published in September or October and feature works that were published during the prior year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical implication for contributors: pieces must appear (or be revised) in the calendar year preceding the anthology edition; editors compile annually and publish the volume in early autumn.
